title: Connection Management in Serverless
description: Strategies for running Prisma in Vercel, AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers using Prisma Accelerate and Driver Adapters.

data.text: Serverless architectures (such as Vercel Functions, AWS Lambda, and Cloudflare Workers) create and destroy execution environments on demand. Traditional databases that expect long-lived TCP connections face two major hurdles in serverless environments: **connection exhaustion** caused by horizontal scaling spikes, and **cold start latency** caused by loading database drivers and initializing TLS handshakes.
Modern Solutions for Prisma in Serverless

cards.title: Prisma Driver Adapters (@prisma/adapter-pg)
cards.description: Offloads networking from the Rust binary to pure JavaScript drivers (like `@neondatabase/serverless` or `pg`) via WebSockets or HTTP.
pros: Runs on Cloudflare Workers and Edge runtimes

cards.title: Prisma Accelerate
cards.description: A managed global connection pool and edge caching layer hosted by Prisma.
pros: Global connection pooling across all cloud regions

cards.title: External Pooler (Neon / Supabase / AWS RDS Proxy)
cards.description: Self-managed or cloud-provider PgBouncer instance sitting directly in front of PostgreSQL.
pros: Keeps architecture within your own cloud VPC

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Serverless cold starts and connection limits require specialized connection strategies.
Use Driver Adapters (`@prisma/adapter-neon` or `@prisma/adapter-pg`) for edge compatibility.
Always reuse the client singleton in `lib/prisma.ts` to share connection pools across warm lambdas.
